label: def:higher-forms
title: Higher differential forms
html:
Definition. Higher differential forms

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe with differential calculus \Omega^1(A). The higher differential forms are the graded A-bimodule:

  \Omega^k(A) =  \bigwedge\nolimits_A^k \Omega^1(A), \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots

Here \Omega^0(A) = A. For an object V, \Lambda^k V denotes its k-th exterior power. The differential d \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A) extends the universal derivation by the graded Leibniz rule and satisfies d^2 = 0:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:de-rham-complex}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  A = \Omega^0(A) \ar[r, "d"]
  & \Omega^1(A) \ar[r, "d"]
  & \Omega^2(A) \ar[r, "d"]
  & \cdots
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad (d^2 = 0)
\end{equation}
